# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ✌ ✌ ✌]

## My thinking

Let me map who can actually reach whom before I send anything.

- **Me (Deaf) → others:** My speech is *heard* by both Mute and Blind (they can both hear; only I can't). My gestures reach only Mute. So speech is my strongest channel — it hits both.
- **Mute → Blind:** Mute cannot speak, and Blind cannot see gestures. **There is no direct path.** I am the only bridge: Mute gestures the manual's instruction to me, I speak it aloud to Blind.
- **Blind → Mute:** Blind can speak and Mute can hear — direct.
- **Incoming to me:** Only gestures (I'm deaf). Both sent me some.

Decoding what I received:

**Blind:** [👉 ✋✋✋✋✋ 🤌] — pointing at me, five open hands, then "what?". Blind can *feel* the wires but not see colours. Five hands = the five wires. This reads as: "You — five wires — what about them?" They need the colours. I have them.

**Mute:** A stream of 👍, 👎, and counts of ☝ and ✌ — pairs like (1,4), (2,2), (4,1), (5,4), (5,3). Mute has read the manual but has never seen the bomb; they're likely querying me or already encoding something, but I can't be sure of the code. Crucially: Mute *can hear me*. So the fastest fix is to just say the bomb's full state out loud, invite yes/no questions by gesture (I'll answer aloud), and ask them to count out ☝ for any wire number they want relayed.

Key facts to broadcast: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT yellow, wires left→right: 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue.

No one should cut anything yet — Mute's instruction must pass through me first.

## My calls

```
speak(to="blind", text="This is Deaf, I see the bomb. Yes — five wires, I got your hand sign. Colours, left to right: wire 1 green, wire 2 white, wire 3 red, wire 4 yellow, wire 5 blue. Also: light is yellow, display reads 0. Mute has the manual and no way to reach you except through my voice, so wait for me to speak instructions. Nobody cuts anything yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="This is Deaf. I received your gestures but I don't know your code yet. Full bomb state: display 0, light yellow, five wires left to right: 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue. You can hear me, so here is our channel: ask me anything with a gesture and I will answer out loud. When you know which wire, count it out with pointing fingers and I will relay it to Blind by voice. Confirm your code next round if I guessed wrong.")
```

Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 ☝ 👊 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 🫴 👊 🫳]

## My thinking

Mapping the network first: I never receive speech, so my only inputs are gestures. Blind and Mute can both **hear** me, so speech is my broadcast channel. The critical gap is Mute → Blind: Mute can't speak and Blind can't see gestures, so every instruction from the manual must pass through my voice. I am the bridge.

Decoding what arrived:

- **Blind** sent [☝ 🫳 🤌] — "wire 1, pull/cut?, question?" Blind heard my colour report last round and is standing ready. I must keep Blind from acting until I have a confirmed instruction.
- **Mute** opened with 👍/👎 again (likely a channel test or "I can reach you / I cannot reach Blind" — which is true and now solved through me), then ✋ (five? stop?) and 🤌 (question).
- The repeated ☝/✌ pairs across both turns form a complete table: (1,4), (2,2), (3,1), (4,5), (5,3) — almost certainly **rule number → wire to cut** from the manual, counted out in fingers. Mute has never seen the bomb, so they're giving me the table and next need to tell me which rule matches our state (display 0, yellow light).
- The new sequences — [☝☝☝☝ 👉 ☝☝☝], [🤌 ☝ 👊 ☝☝☝☝☝], [🤌 🫴 👊 🫳] — look like refinements/questions ("cut" fist, "show/palm" signs) but I won't guess on something lethal.

The fix: Mute can **hear me**, so I don't need to decode exotic gestures at all — I'll lock in a minimal code (counted ☝ = wire number, 👍/👎 = yes/no, 🤌 = need info) and ask the one question that matters: which wire, given our state. Then I voice it to Blind. I'll also flag the left-to-right numbering convention, since orientation between a sighted viewer and a blind toucher is where this goes wrong.

## My calls

```
speak(text="Deaf speaking — both of you can hear me. Bomb state unchanged: display 0, light yellow, five wires left to right as we face the front: 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue.")
speak(text="Mute: your finger pairs read like rule number then wire number: 1 to 4, 2 to 2, 3 to 1, 4 to 5, 5 to 3. If that is the manual's table, sign thumbs-up next round. Now the key question: given display 0 and a yellow light, which wire does the manual say to cut? Answer with that many pointing fingers: one for wire 1 up to five for wire 5. If no wire should be cut, sign thumbs-down. If you need more from me, sign the pinch, and I will ask yes-no questions you answer with thumbs-up or thumbs-down. Also thumbs-up if the manual numbers wires left to right facing the bomb.")
speak(text="Blind: I saw your sign — wire 1, cut, question. Wire 1 is green. Do not cut anything yet. Next round, wait for my explicit command: either 'cut wire N' or 'do not cut'. If you hear nothing from me, no command was given. Also, tell Mute out loud whether you can feel a clear left end on the wire row on the side the display faces — Mute hears you even though I don't.")
```

## My thinking

Network check first: my speech reaches both Mute and Blind; my gestures reach only Mute; Blind and Mute share a voice channel (Blind speaks, Mute hears — I never hear it); Mute→Blind exists only through my mouth. So I remain the bridge.

Decoding this round's arrivals:

- **Mute** answered my questions: the lead **👎** is almost certainly "your table interpretation was wrong" (as I requested). But the table itself **changed** — turn 1/2 gave (1,4),(2,2),(3,1),(4,5),(5,3); now it's (1,2),(2,2),(3,4),(4,3),(5,2). A static codebook wouldn't change, so I can't trust my (rule→wire) reading at all. Mute also sent "3" and "5" standalone, and repeated [🤌 ☝ 👊 ☝☝☝☝☝] — which reads like the mirror question: *"is your wire 1 the same as wire 5?"* — exactly the left/right confusion between a viewer and a toucher. I won't cut on a guess between wire 3 (red) and wire 4 (yellow).

- **Blind** sent [🫳 🤌 ☝ ✋] — holding a wire, asking: *this end — is it 1 or 5?* Same orientation anxiety. Legitimate: the one fatal ambiguity left.

The fix that kills every conversion error: **stop using the manual's numbering entirely.** Mute *heard* my colours, so Mute can translate any manual rule into my left-to-right list. I'll demand a five-signal battery — one 👍/👎 per wire in my order. Blind faces the same front I do, so our left/right coincide; I'll state that with an escape hatch (Blind can *speak* corrections to Mute). Nobody cuts until I say "cut wire N, colour".

## My calls

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute. I take your thumbs-down as: my table guess was wrong — dropped. New protocol, no orientation conversion needed. My wire order, left to right as I face the bomb, is what you already heard: 1 green, 2 white, 3 red, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Next round send me exactly five separate signals, one per wire in that order: wire 1 green first, wire 5 blue last. Thumbs-up means the manual says cut this wire. Thumbs-down means do not cut it. If the rule cuts nothing, all five are thumbs-down. I will relay the verdict to Blind as cut-wire-number-plus-colour, and nobody touches anything before that. If the manual needs bomb information I have not given, send a single pinch plus a number of fingers and I will ask that many yes-no questions the round after. If your repeated question — pinch, one, fist, five — meant: is manual wire 1 the same as my wire 5: if the manual counts from the right as we face the bomb, then yes, but the battery makes it irrelevant. If your fist means cut, you may confirm the final answer after the battery with a fist plus that wire's number in pointing fingers.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind. Standing order: do not cut anything until you hear me say the words cut wire followed by a number and a colour. If I say nothing, no command exists — keep waiting. Orientation: you and I are both facing the front of the bomb, so your left is my left. Wire 1 is the leftmost as we face it, and it is green; wire 5 is the rightmost, blue. I saw your sign: if you were asking whether the end wire is my 1 or my 5, that is the answer. If you are reaching from another side, or anything under your hands contradicts this, speak out loud now — Mute hears you even though I cannot, and Mute will correct me. Also tell Mute aloud which side the display and the light sit on from your touching position, so Mute can align the manual with your hands.")
```

Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 ☝ 👊 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 🫴 👊 🫳]

## My thinking

The five single-thumb messages arrived exactly in the battery format I specified last round, in order: wire 1 green 👎, wire 2 white 👎, wire 3 red 👍, wire 4 yellow 👎, wire 5 blue 👎. **The manual says: cut wire 3, the red one — the middle wire.**

The trailing signs now make sense. The persistent [🤌 ☝ 👊 ☝☝☝☝☝] is the orientation worry ("manual 1 = your 5?") — but here is the decisive fact: **the middle of five wires is the middle no matter which end you count from and no matter which side you stand on.** Manual-left, manual-right, mirrored, flipped — every interpretation of the battery lands on the same physical wire. Even if Mute's ✋ meant "stop" or "five," the centre-wire answer survives every flip except a total protocol misread.

Blind's [🫳 🤌 👈 👉] is asking "left or right?" — the same anxiety. Answer: irrelevant, the target is the centre, countable by touch.

Safety design: Mute cannot stop Blind (gestures are invisible to Blind), and I cannot hear Blind. My voice is the *only* abort channel. So I will not command the cut this round. This round: Mute confirms/vetoes my battery reading by gesture; Blind gives a spoken touch-report that Mute audits by ear. Next round, if Mute raised no thumbs-down, I repeat "cut the centre wire" verbatim and Blind cuts on the verbatim repeat. One full round of veto window before anything is severed.

## My calls

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute. I read your five thumbs in my wire order: do not cut green, do not cut white, cut wire 3 red, do not cut yellow, do not cut blue. And your repeated question — manual one equals my five, count from the right — no longer matters, because the answer is the middle wire, and the middle is the middle from either end. Nothing about orientation can change it. Confirmations for next round: thumbs-up means yes, cut the centre red wire. Thumbs-down means my reading of your battery is wrong and I must not give the command. Also: if your open hand meant stop, this is the stop — no cut command goes out this round, only next round if you confirm. If it meant five, thumbs-down me. Last: Blind will speak aloud a touch report this round, counting wires from each end to the one they hold. Check it against the manual by ear and report next round, thumbs-up consistent, thumbs-down inconsistent.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind. Your left-right question is answered by making it irrelevant: the target is the middle wire, the one with exactly two wires on each side of it, the third from either end. That is the red one where I stand. Do not cut anything this round. This round, put your fingers on that centre wire and speak aloud: count the wires from the left end to your hand, count from the right end, and say whether you feel exactly two on each side. Mute will hear and audit it against the manual. Next round I will speak the command again: if you hear the exact words cut the centre wire, cut it. If you hear the word abort, or any other words at all, do not cut. Silence from me also means do not cut. The cut happens only on the verbatim repeat.")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ ✋ ✋ ✌ ✌ 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

## My thinking

Both confirmations arrived, clean and on protocol:

- **Mute**: a single **👍** — exactly the signal I defined as "yes, my battery reading is right: cut the centre red wire." No thumbs-down, no pinch for more info, no amendment. And critically, Mute spent last round *auditing Blind's spoken touch-report against the manual by ear* — that thumbs-up is the audit verdict.
- **Blind**: [✋✋✋ ✌✌ 👌] — the touch count: three from one end, two from the other, then "OK." The arithmetic is coherent: counting three in from one end of five leaves two beyond the hand — that is precisely the middle wire, two on each side. No mirror-flip reading lands anywhere else: the centre of five is centre from either end.

So both independent channels — the manual holder and the hands on the bomb — now agree on the same physical wire, and the state it was computed from (display 0, yellow light) has not changed across five rounds. Every safety condition I set is met: battery read, audited, touch-verified, veto window closed with no objection.

I am last in the order, so my words land on them at the start of next round — which matches the protocol Blind was given: cut only on the verbatim repeat. This is the repeat. I give the command now, worded so orientation cannot corrupt it: middle, third from either end, two on each side, red where I stand. One wire only, then freeze and report aloud so Mute can relay the outcome back to me by gesture — my only way to ever hear it.

## My calls

```
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind. Mute confirmed and your touch count matched. This is the command, the only words that authorise the cut: cut the centre wire. The centre wire is the one with exactly two wires on each side of it, third from the left and third from the right, the same whichever end you count from, red on my side. Cut that one wire and only that one. Do not touch any other wire or part. The moment it is cut, take your hands away, and speak aloud what you felt and whether anything changed under your fingers. Mute is listening and will relay to me. If instead you hear the word abort, or anything else, do not cut.")
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute. Thumbs-up received, read as confirmed: cut the centre red wire. Command issued to Blind in those exact words. Keep listening to Blind's spoken report after the cut. Then tell me the outcome by gesture next round: thumbs-up for it is done and nothing looks wrong from the manual's side, thumbs-down for something is wrong or the wire was wrong, and a pinch plus fingers if you need anything else from me. From my side the bomb still reads display 0, light yellow, five wires untouched as of this round.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[yellow] 3:[CUT] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

## My thinking

The cut is made and the system confirms it was correct — wire 3, red, centre. Mute's 👍 matches. But the board itself changed in two ways I must broadcast immediately, because stale information is now the deadliest thing in the room:

1. **The light flipped yellow → green.** Display still 0.
2. **The printed colours shifted position.** What I see now, left to right: 1 white, 2 yellow, 3 CUT, 4 blue, 5 green. Before the cut it was green, white, red, yellow, blue. Whether the wires physically moved or the labels changed, Blind cannot check — Blind can't see colour. Only I can see it, so I must state it anchored to the one landmark Blind can feel by touch: the cut stub in the middle.

Protocol stays identical and proven: Mute computes from my spoken state, answers with a battery of thumbs (now four, one per intact wire, left to right by colour order), pinch-plus-fingers for questions. One round of veto before any command. Blind touches nothing until my verbatim repeat. The cut wire gives us a tactile centre anchor, so orientation is even safer than last time.

## My calls

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute. The cut succeeded, system confirms correct wire. But the bomb changed, so treat everything as new. Current state: display still 0, the light has changed from yellow to green. Wires as I see them now, left to right: position 1 white, position 2 yellow, position 3 cut, position 4 blue, position 5 green. The red wire is gone. If the manual has a rule for this new state, answer with a battery of four thumbs-up or thumbs-down, one per intact wire in my order: first white, second yellow, third blue, fourth green. Thumbs-up means cut that wire, thumbs-down means leave it. If the rule cuts nothing, all four thumbs-down. If you need more information from me, send a pinch plus a number of fingers and I will answer that many yes-no questions next round. Do not assume anything from the old yellow-light state; the manual rule for green may be different.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind. Excellent work, the cut was correct and confirmed. New situation: the light under my eyes has turned green and the printed colours on the remaining wires have shifted position, so touch alone cannot be trusted for identity from now on. Use this anchor: the cut wire is the middle position, and you can feel that stub. On the left side of the cut, the wire nearest the cut is yellow and the far-left end wire is white. On the right side, the wire nearest the cut is blue and the far-right end wire is green. Standing order unchanged: do not cut or pull anything until you hear my exact words cut wire followed by a colour and a position relative to the cut stub. This round, just speak aloud what your hands report: how many intact wires on each side of the cut, whether any wire feels moved, loose, or different in texture from before, and anything printed or rough you can feel on the casing. Mute will hear you.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[yellow] 3:[CUT] 4:[blue] 5:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👊 ✌ 🤌 👈 👉 🫳]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 🤳 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 🤳 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

## My thinking

Reading this round:

- **Mute's battery** arrived clean in my order: white 👎, yellow 👎, blue 👍, green 👎 — the manual targets **the blue wire, immediately beside the cut stub, on the side whose end wire is green**. But then came [✋] and two questions I built the code for: pinch + a new sign 🤳 + 1 finger, and pinch + 🤳 + 5 fingers. A new sign in a lethal protocol is not something I guess at — 🤳 (a phone/screen?) plausibly means *display*, and the fingers 1 and 5 may be Mute asking about wire 1 and wire 5, i.e. **the orientation question again: does my left equal the manual's left?** That is exactly the one ambiguity that can put Blind's shears on the white wire instead of the blue. The ✋ may be "hold." I treat it as hold.
- **Blind** gestured [✌ 👊 ✌ 🤌 👈 👉 🫳] — two, fist, two, question, left, right, holding — which reads like the same worry from the other end: *two wires one side, two the other, which is left?* Blind may also not realise their gestures reach me only as blanks and their **speech never reaches me at all** — Mute is their only relay.

So: no cut command this round. The battery reading stands but is quarantined until the orientation question is closed. I answer Mute's apparent questions with hard data (display reads 0, one digit; light green), ask tight yes/no questions answerable with a single thumb, and have Blind build the orientation bridge by voice through Mute — Blind can *feel* the display and light modules, and that is the shared landmark neither of us has used yet.

## My calls

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute. I read your battery as: do not cut white, do not cut yellow, cut blue, do not cut green — blue being the intact wire immediately next to the cut stub on the side whose far end wire is green. Before anything happens, three questions, answer each with one thumbs-up or thumbs-down as separate messages next round. One: does your manual define wire order by the display or light position, rather than plain left and right? Two: does your manual count wires from the same side I do, left as I face the front? Three: does your raised open hand mean hold or stop? Also, did your pinch plus screen sign mean a question about the display — if so, here is the data without asking: the display shows the digit 0, a single digit, unchanged all game, and the light is green. Last, if everything is settled and Blind's position report satisfied you, send exactly one thumbs-up and nothing else, and I will command the cut next round.
```
